writing.overall_comment: A solid, well-scoped Java backend agent, but it needs explicit hand-back boundaries and de-duplication to fit the token budget.

dimensions.name: Delegation fit
dimensions.comment: Description clearly names the tech stack and purpose, letting a main agent route Java/Spring tasks, though it doesn't differentiate from adjacent backend or API-design agents.

dimensions.name: Prompt quality
dimensions.comment: Role, expertise areas, security/quality constraints, and a step-by-step code-generation workflow are explicit and actionable.

dimensions.name: Boundaries
dimensions.comment: Has a do/don't list and a strong 'reuse existing dependencies' rule, but never states what the agent must not do or when to hand back to the main agent (e.g., frontend, DevOps, unclear requirements).

dimensions.name: Conciseness
dimensions.comment: Prompt is bloated with heavy repetition—dependency management, layering, and transaction rules appear three-plus times across principles, best practices, and do/don't sections.

suggestions: Add an explicit out-of-scope/hand-back subsection to the agent prompt that states when to return to the main agent for frontend, DevOps, or unclear requirements, since Boundaries scored 0.5.
Consolidate the repeated dependency-management, layering, and transaction rules into a single section of the prompt to remove three-plus duplications and improve Conciseness.
Revise the agent description to distinguish Java/Spring backend implementation from adjacent backend or API-design agents so the main agent can route more precisely.
